extracted.intended_audience: General readers and prospective book buyers (businessmen, farmers, literary men, young men, students, women, politicians, and booksellers)
extracted.subtask_description: Promotional/advertisement page for Horace Greeley's autobiography collecting publisher copy and multiple press reviews that evaluate the book's content, production, audience, and likely reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autobiographical character
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The present volume, accordingly, is the first production on the subject which can claim an autobiographical character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as the author's own recollections and 'mental history' with 'small reserve' — the book's value is tied to being a first-person, authentic autobiographical record rather than a third‑party biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical execution / physical production quality
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The mechanical execution of the work is highly creditable... It is printed on type and paper of unusual excellence, and the binding is at once substantial and elegant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates typography, paper quality, binding, and overall physical attractiveness; reviewers repeatedly call it a 'handsome volume' and praise the publishers' workmanship as part of its merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and portrait quality
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Illustrated with the best Steel Portrait of Mr. Greeley ever published... together with a beautiful Portrait of Margaret Fuller, engraved by Linton.' 'The portrait of Mr. Greeley... is a striking likeness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality engravings/portraits are highlighted as increasing interest and value; specific engravers and likeness fidelity are noted as important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended readership / audience relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher copy: 'a book to be read with interest by Business Men, Farmers, Literary Men, Young Men, Students of the Times, the Women of America, Politicians, Men of the South, Northern Loyalists, Intelligent Thinkers of all Classes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses who will benefit from or be interested in the book; reviewers echo that all classes of American readers and especially young men and students will find value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and political value / contribution to political history
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews note 'copious reminiscences of the political developments of the last twenty-five years,' 'a valuable summary of political developments,' and 'a contribution to politics as well as to the cause of self-culture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values the book as a primary-source account of recent political history, useful for understanding public men and measures; judged on the informational/historical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and narrative style
rubrics_metrics.description: Review phrasing: 'frank, straight-forward, racily told story of his own career,' 'chatty volume,' 'interesting on every page,' 'delightful one.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses tone, pacing, and how engaging the prose is — e.g., frankness, raciness, chatty/anecdotal style — as measures of literary merit and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional and moral value
rubrics_metrics.description: Review claims: 'full of instruction and hope,' 'a moral tonic,' 'abound in anecdotes, in humor, and wise counsel,' and 'instructive to boys and young men.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges the book on its capacity to instruct, inspire, or serve as moral/example literature for youth and families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotal richness and human interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple reviews stress anecdotes and reminiscences: 'abound in anecdotes, in humor, and wise counsel,' 'gives... stories of his past campaigns,' 'how eagerly we ask him about the actors who have long since left the stage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures the value of illustrative stories, personal reminiscences, and memorable episodes that make the narrative engaging and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness / scope of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher summary: 'The book embraces views of early New England settlement, the author's own youthful life, education, apprenticeship, adventures, professional and political reminiscences, experience in Congress, newspaper-life in New York, and much useful talk about farms and farming.' Reviewers call it 'a pretty full history of the country for those years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses breadth of topics covered and whether the volume offers a wide-ranging picture of life, politics, and times — usefulness as a multi‑topic memoir.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Review statements: 'a pretty full, and doubtless a very accurate, autobiography' and 'valuable as a truthful record of the career of one of the most remarkable men in America.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers factual reliability and honesty of self‑reporting; reviewers explicitly judge the work as accurate and truthful, boosting its credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial appeal and sales potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher note and reviews: 'We venture to predict for this book a large sale.' 'Began by selling furiously in the Middle and New England States... we predict a broader and an enduring demand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates marketability based on subject popularity, prior serial success, topical interest, and controversy (e.g., mentions of the 'bailing' incident affecting sales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for family or general household readership
rubrics_metrics.description: 'As a moral tonic, we have seldom seen a book that we would more readily place in the hands of a family... a book to be read with interest by... the Women of America.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges appropriateness for family reading, edifying content, and broad domestic appeal (fit as a gift or household book).
